knowledge_point.title: Rewriting a Double Integral Over a Circle or Part-Circle Not Centered at the Origin

question.:question/problem:
Let $D=\{(x,y):x^{2}+(y+3)^{2}\leq9\}$. The disk is shown below.

![Disk](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/edb-math/repairs/2026-10-29-matrix-outer-fences/generator-probes/17592186129275-easy/f2ff3cadb4bdae8ee2e9.png)

Its outer circular boundary has polar equation $r=- 6 \sin{\left(\theta \right)}$. Use $x=r\cos\theta$, $y=r\sin\theta$, and $\mathrm{d}A=r\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta$. Rewrite

$$
\iint_D 1\,\mathrm{d}A.
$$

Select the polar-coordinate setup whose bounds cover $D$ once with $r\geq0$ and whose integrand includes the area factor. Do not evaluate the integral.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use $x=r\cos\theta$, $y=r\sin\theta$, and $\mathrm{d}A=r\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta$. The full disk has radius $3$ and center $(0,-3)$.

**Radial bounds.** Expanding the disk inequality gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x^2+y^2+6y&\leq0\\r^2+6r\sin{\left(\theta \right)}&\leq0\\r(r-(- 6 \sin{\left(\theta \right)}))&\leq0.\end{aligned}
$$

For $r>0$, divide by $r$; the origin is included as well. Thus $0\leq r\leq - 6 \sin{\left(\theta \right)}$.

**Angular bounds.** The upper radial bound must be nonnegative. The full disk permits $\pi\leq\theta\leq2 \pi$. Choose $\pi\leq\theta\leq2 \pi$. Every interior point is covered once.

![Region, representative radial segment and angular sweep](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/edb-math/repairs/2026-10-29-matrix-outer-fences/generator-probes/17592186129275-easy/c53e83a6cfe95cb4d300.png)

**Transformed integrand.** The density substitution and area factor give

$$
\begin{aligned}1&=1\\1\,\mathrm{d}A&=r\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore the required setup is

$$
\displaystyle\int_{\pi}^{2 \pi}\int_{0}^{- 6 \sin{\left(\theta \right)}}r\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta.
$$

**Other choices.** $\displaystyle\int_{\pi}^{2 \pi}\int_{0}^{- 6 \sin{\left(\theta \right)}}1\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta$: The area factor is missing. $\displaystyle\int_{- \frac{\pi}{2}}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\int_{0}^{6 \cos{\left(\theta \right)}}r\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta$: These bounds describe a different disk or part-disk, with a different center direction. $\displaystyle\int_{\pi}^{2 \pi}\int_{0}^{3}r^{2}\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta$: The center-to-boundary radius is incorrectly used as a constant polar upper bound. The area factor was squared instead of used once. $\displaystyle\int_{\pi}^{2 \pi}\int_{0}^{3}1\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta$: The center-to-boundary radius is incorrectly used as a constant polar upper bound. The area factor is missing.
